lastPrompt: # Task: condense Apple's and Microsoft's desktop UI guidelines into rules for the Kvit apps  ## Background  Kvit is a set of cross-platform desktop applications written in Go: kvit-cash (/home/sk/kvit…

aiTitle: Apple and Microsoft UI guidelines for Kvit

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'kvit-ui-guidelines-consolidate',
  description: 'Fold the Windows 7 guide records into the merged rules, one agent per topic family, keeping the total at 200 or fewer',
  phases: [{ title: 'Consolidate', detail: '6 agents, one per family of rule prefixes' }],
}
const S = args.scratch
const P = (g) => `You are merging UI guidelines into rules for Kvit, a family of cross-platform desktop apps (Windows, macOS, Linux) in Go that draw with one component library, kvit-ui (/home/user/kvit-ui; read its CLAUDE.md). Apple's HIG has already been merged into draft rules; Microsoft's Windows 7 UX guide has been extracted and partly mapped onto them. Your job: finish the merge for the rule prefixes ${g.prefixes.join(', ')}.

The owner's decisions (apply, do not reopen): the apps behave as close to each platform's defaults as possible; where Apple and Microsoft differ, a rule has a Windows form and a macOS form and the app uses the one for the system it runs on; Linux uses the Windows form (note it when the choice matters there); visual appearance is not taken (Kvit has its own look, themes, Phosphor icons); menus are the system's own on macOS and Kvit-drawn on Windows and Linux. Microsoft's current Fluent guidance could not be fetched, so the Windows 7 guide is the only Windows source; say so in a Windows form only when it matters.

Input: ${S}/consol/in-${g.n}.json with
- "rules": the draft merged rules for your prefixes (id, title, example, win, mac, plat, src, enf [[kind,text]] with kinds component/test-source/test-screen/test-app/review, now [status,text] with status enforces/partly/contradicts/none). A "win" value starting "Not sourced yet" is a placeholder to replace with the Windows form from the Windows records, or with null when Windows agrees with the general rule.
- "notes": Windows records already mapped to one of your rules that carry a note: "WIN-FORM: …" (Windows does it differently: put this in the rule's win form, set plat true) or "CONFLICT: …" (decide: either the rule becomes platform-specific with both forms, or the rule changes, or it is an owner decision — then add an open question).
- "new": Windows records (topic in your family) that matched no draft rule, each with a short "title" the extractor gave; many share a title. "checklist": true means the item is on Microsoft's own top-violations checklist and deserves weight.
Also available: ${S}/rule-index.txt (every draft rule of every prefix, for mapping into other families), ${S}/consol/kvit-ui-survey.md (what kvit-ui does today with file:line; verify any claim you add against the code in /home/user/kvit-ui).
Records already mapped to a rule without a note are added to that rule's sources automatically; you need not list them.

Do:
1. For every "new" record, map it to a rule: one of yours (existing or new), or any id in rule-index.txt from another family when it fits there better. Prefer folding into an existing rule (widen its wording slightly) over creating a rule. A record that is a detail of a broader rule maps to that rule.
2. You may create at most ${g.budget} new rules in your prefixes (ids continue each prefix's numbering), and you may fold existing rules of yours into one another to make room (record it). Your family's final rule count must be at most ${g.cap}. New rules go to what matters most: checklist items, Windows conventions Kvit must follow (access keys, OK/Cancel semantics, sentence case, message structure, notification area, etc.), and anything the five problem areas need: sentences on buttons, letters instead of icons, one command under several names / one icon for several actions, generic labels (OK), permanent explanations and missing shortcuts.
3. Update each rule's win/mac forms and plat flag from the notes and records. Keep a rule's text in plain short sentences, rule first, an example where it helps. Keep existing text when nothing changes.
4. For every rule you create or change materially, fill enf and now accurately: what kvit-ui does today with file:line (check the code), and where the rule should be enforced (component named and what changes; or a test and what it reads: Go source, one screen's list of controls with roles and names, or all screens of an app together; or review).
5. Collect open questions: where a source contradicts itself or another source, or leaves a case undefined, or the owner must choose (each with the options, what each would change, and your recommendation, and the ids involved). Also list every rule where applying the Windows form on Linux matters.

Output: write ${S}/consol/out-${g.n}.json (never write inside /home/user/kvit-ui) as {"rules":[...same shape as input rules, all your family's final rules, src as full ids — keep the existing src and add the Windows record ids you mapped to it ...], "folded": {"OLD-ID": "TARGET-ID"}, "map": {"<every new record id>": "<rule id>"}, "open_questions": [{"title":…, "ids":[…], "options":[…], "changes":…, "recommendation":…}], "linux": ["RULE-ID: why the Windows form matters on Linux", …]}.
Validate with python3 -I: every new record id is in map; every map target is one of your final ids or an id in rule-index.txt not folded; your rule count ≤ ${g.cap}; every rule has title, src, enf, now. Return a short summary: counts, rules created and folded, and the open questions' titles.`

const G = [
  { n: 1, prefixes: ['WRD'], budget: 4, cap: 29 },
  { n: 2, prefixes: ['CTL', 'LAY'], budget: 3, cap: 35 },
  { n: 3, prefixes: ['MSG', 'FDB'], budget: 3, cap: 27 },
  { n: 4, prefixes: ['KEY', 'PTR', 'A11Y'], budget: 3, cap: 38 },
  { n: 5, prefixes: ['WIN', 'CMD'], budget: 3, cap: 50 },
  { n: 6, prefixes: ['HLP', 'CON', 'OTH'], budget: 1, cap: 21 },
]
phase('Consolidate')
return await parallel(G.map(g => () => agent(P(g), { label: `consolidate ${g.prefixes.join('/')}`, phase: 'Consolidate' })))
